turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your hip replacement surgery. Can you tell me a bit about why you're having this surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Morning, doctor. My right hip been hurting a lot, especially when walking. X-ray show severe arthritis, so doctor say need to replace it lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Let's go through your medications. I see you're on quite a few – can you confirm what you're currently taking?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. I take Amlodipine 5mg every day for blood pressure, Metformin 500mg twice daily for diabetes, Insulin glargine 20 units at night. Furosemide 20mg only when I have swelling, Tamsulosin for prostate, Aspirin 75mg daily, Pantoprazole 40mg daily, and Atorvastatin 20mg nightly.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Have there been any changes to your medications in the last year, particularly with your acid suppression medication?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh yes! I stopped Ranitidine about six months ago because of that big recall news. My GP switched me to Pantoprazole 40mg daily since then.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for clarifying that. Are all your other medications still the same doses as listed?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, doctor. Everything else same as before. Only the Ranitidine changed to Pantoprazole.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good to know. Any allergies we should know about?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I get a rash from Penicillin. That's the only one.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Noted. Have you had any previous anesthesia or surgeries?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Had a spinal block for my cataract surgery last year. No problems at all, very smooth.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. What about your fasting status today?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I had a light breakfast around 6am, nothing since 8am. Just some water for meds lah.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect. Finally, how's your mobility before surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Can walk with a cane, but pain makes it difficult. Need help with stairs sometimes.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you for all that information, Mr. Tan. We'll be using general anesthesia with spinal anesthesia for pain control during surgery. Any questions for me?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No questions, doctor. Just want to get this done and walk properly again.
